Once baked it will look something like this: Fresh mozzarella is added after the pizza is baked - or towards the end of the baking process, and results in this: The history of ‘dry’ mozzarella is pretty interesting: it was invented in the States and initially snubbed by Italians who, rightfully, claimed it wasn’t mozzarella. Since the product is ideal for baking pizzas, they then re-invented that same product and now use it in most pizzerias and at home. It’s a weird world.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the recipe for making butter and garlic sauce for pasta from scratch?
Answer: Pasta with butter, garlic and anchovy is an easy yet pleasing dish to prepare As you are going to fry your garlic and anchovy, better use clarified butter. Anyway, once you fried your ingredients, add your pasta and a ladle of cooking water. Stir and serve straight away.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is a chicken salad recipe?
Answer: Though I have no idea who came up with this recipe -as it is not very Italian- it is quite popular here in Sicily. Shredded boiled chicken, lettuce, finely sliced celery and some olives topped off with a mayonnaise and ketchup mix, locally known as pink sauce. It sometimes comes with fresh tomato. Nice comfort food indeed.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do you make risotto less bland?
Answer: In other words, how to make it tasty. Use a good broth and don’t be stingy with the parmigiano cheese and butter.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How can leftover pieces of hard or stale bread be used in other ways?
Answer: A personal favourite is turning it into polpette di pane, bread balls. And I confess that some of our bread is purposely set aside in order to prepare them. Here is how you prepare them. First pour some milk over your stale bread. Let it absorb slowly, no need for drowning. Then add an egg, grated cheese and seasoning to your likes. Salt, pepper and nutmeg for us. Roll the dough in little balls and fry them. Baking is an option. Have them as a snack, an aperitif or just because.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is the type of water used to cook pasta important for its taste? If yes, what types of water are recommended for making pasta?
Answer: The type of water, as long as it is potable, doesn’t change the outcome of your pasta. The water is first of all brought to a boil, after which it is salted. Once pasta is boiled, it is added to a condiment or sauce.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What Indian dish blew your mind when you tasted it for the first time?
Answer: Somewhere in the early eighties my dad took me to an Indian restaurant in Neal street, probably overstating my culinary curiosity. The Punjabi cuisine, he assured my mom, wasn’t all that hot. She and my sister stayed home anyway. The Punjabi cuisine may not be as hot as the southern Indian one, but being the introduction to spicy food, it seemed hell to me. It took a lot on naan and lassi to ease the burning. Their murgh makhani, butter chicken, was so spectacularly good I mopped the last sauce from the plate, while tears ran down my cheeks. My love for that dish never ceased. Until today I’m extremely grateful to my dad -who had no recollection of taking me there when I recently asked him. By the way, the restaurant is still there.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do you select the best quality seafood for cooking?
Answer: I am far from an expert but can rely on a trusted fishmonger, signor Paolo, at the Ballarò market. The difference between a fishmonger and a trusted fishmonger is significant over here. He’ll tell you what fish to buy and especially what fish not to buy. In a very subtle way. For example by lightly shaking his head when ordering some fish. Or in a funny way, like that morning when I took the picture, he told me there was no swordfish.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Do you cook every night? Why?
Answer: When home, I do. Usually in good company of my kids. Why? Because it’s nice to spend time together, helping each other out. And when crowned with a lovely meal, what more can you wish for? Cooking relaxes me and never strikes as a duty. It furthermore allows control over what you eat and health in general.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Lunchroom debate to be settled: Is cheese on a tuna sandwich a good idea, bad idea, or does it depend on the cheese? Is there a cheese to avoid?
Answer: There is an unwritten rule in Italy stating that fish and cheese should not be combined, especially when it comes to pasta. There has been some debate about this, where apparently young university students do add parmesan cheese to their beloved pasta al tonno. In a discussion a renowned chef told that he wouldn’t serve that even to his dog. To which the brilliant answer was that his dog didn’t go to university. Anyway, cheese can go on a tuna sandwich if it’s an accompanying cheese, not a contrasting cheese. Avoid seasoned and strong cheese, welcome soft ones. Cottage cheese, ricotta (ok, technically not a cheese) or mozzarella are fine.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What makes pine nuts special in pesto? Can almonds be used as a substitute?
Answer: The ubiquitous green pesto, Genovese, is made with pine nuts. Mainly because pine nuts grow profusely in Liguria. They are pretty unctuous and quite mild in taste, with a hint of resin. It may seem pendantic, but not even imported pine nuts should be used, let alone other kinds of nuts. Pesto is a pricy recipe; the olive oil, pine nuts and cheese weigh in on the cost. When you find cheap jars in the supermarket bearing the name pesto, it is an imitation, usually a very poor one. Now you can use other nuts when making other kinds of pesto. As pesto alla Trapanese for example. Instead of pine nuts it uses almonds (as almond trees grow profusely in Sicily).

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you suggest a quick and easy recipe that can be cooked in under 20 minutes?
Answer: Most pasta dishes can be prepared under twenty minutes. It usually starts with putting a pot of water on the stove before preparing the sauce or condiment. Like the pasta we had a couple of hours ago. A little butter, lemon zest and juice heated in a pan and mixed with fresh boiled spaghetti.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Why is olive oil now more expensive than many wines?
Answer: On average a bottle of olive oil will cost more than a bottle of wine. The main difference is that a bottle of wine will last for an evening, a bottle of olive oil for a month or more.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are the side effects of olive oil and lemon juice?
Answer: It bothers me somehow when people have to dig for possible flaws when dealing with overall healthy products. Usually it all boils down to quantity: yes six kilo of apples a day ain’t healthy, drinking ten litres of water, not a good idea etc. But since you’re asking: too much olive oil makes you fat, causes skin rashes and increases your risk on a hearth attack. Too much lemon ruins your teeth and causes constipation. What is too much? More than four table spoons per day for olive oil; more than the juice of one and a half lemon.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How can the strong taste of garlic be minimized in cooking, aside from using less or choosing a less potent type?
Answer: You can soak garlic cloves overnight in milk. Don’t forget to rinse them. Though the milk is usually discarded, some drink it. You boil your cloves of garlic. Not just once, but three times, changing the water. Five minutes each time. Parsley mitigates garlic perfectly well. In the Italian cuisine they are often found together.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What ingredients can be added to Risotto without significantly altering its taste?
Answer: Very fancy but all that spectacular is risotto with prosecco. Good white wine, as normally used when preparing risotto, tastes similar if not the same.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do you prepare pasta with veggies such as broccoli? Do you need cream?
Answer: Cream made its entry in the Italian savoury cuisine somewhere in the eighties. Dishes like pasta with salmon, vodka and cream represented the opulence of that time. Another classic, pasta with ham, peas and cream (in Italian this sounds way better, with an amazing alliteration: pasta con panna prosciutto e piselli) is comfort food even today. Anyway, the cream craze waned and new techniques to make pasta dishes creamier was introduced: using the starchy water your pasta boiled in and a thorough mix indeed makes your pasta creamy without having to rely on actual cream. If you please to have creamy broccoli, blend your boiled (or steamed) vegetables with some olive oil, grated cheese and seasoning. This procedures works with many other vegetables. Artichokes, zucchini, peas, asparagus etc.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Do you enjoy experimenting with fusion cuisine?
Answer: I am a sucker when it comes to buying exotic ingredients. Shrimp paste from Thailand, Canadian maple syrup, Chinese black bean paste etc. Though rather reluctant to introduce foreign ingredients in the Italian cuisine, sometimes it is well worth it. A dash of Vietnamese fish sauce may find its way into a pasta with tuna. When I cook for myself.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Why do some Italians prefer their food to be referred to as "Italian cuisine" or "Italian dishes" instead of just "pasta"?
Answer: When dining out in Italy, restaurants that serve Italian food are just restaurants. What does often happen is that, mainly in the bigger cities, a restaurant serves regional food. When that region is different from the one you find yourself in, they well state that. Like this Roman restaurant in Milano Or a Sicilian restaurant in Rome

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do I make a simple salad dressing?
Answer: That’s the time you can use that special bottle of olive oil you bought. Just a drizzle of liquid gold, a pinch of salt and you’re done. Some origano and or vinegar/lemon juice if you please. Avoid store bought dressings at any cost. They cover the taste of your ingredients and cancel the health benefits of having a salad.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it common for waitstaff at Italian restaurants to bring out the bill before asking for dessert orders?
Answer: That could happen, yes, but it is not common. When people had a large meal the restaurant may offer dessert, coffee or a digestive drink. The waiting staff will be order to communicate the happy news but usually before bringing the bill to the table. As it goes in other countries, the practice goes that diners ask for the bill. Bringing the bill before that moment is altogether rather rude.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you suggest a type of fish that is mild in taste, easy to cook without bones, and also healthy?
Answer: Not they prettiest one swimming in the sea, but it suits your request perfectly: monkfish The tail is fleshy and contains no bones and actually resembles chicken breast. Don’t throw the rest away is the head and other parts make an excellent fish broth. Monkfish is very delicate in taste, so avoid heavy sauces or frying. Add some cherry tomatoes, olives and capers and oven bake. Easy, fast and healthy.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the packing method used for tuna?
Answer: In times gone by tuna fishing was a seasonable business in Sicily. In early summer specialised fishermen, lead by a rais, set up a series of nets, driving a float of tuna together in a central net. More than fished the tuna was then harpooned, a practice known as la mattanza Not a pretty sight. The tuna was then brought to a factory, a tonnara where the fish was cut up and boiled in salted water before being jarred. The jars were topped off with olive oil. Not because of the particular taste of olive oil, but simply because that was the only oil available. The business was good and some families became extremely rich running it. The tonnare today are no longer used to process tuna. Some of them were restored and used to host parties and weddings. Today most of the tuna is fished all year round, in all parts of the world, and canned rather than jarred. There are surely advantages to canning tuna, the main one is the extended shelf life. The adding of oil is no longer a necessity but rather a reminder of the past.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some alternatives to ground beef that can be used in spaghetti sauce and/or lasagna for protein?
Answer: What about pasta with chicken liver? It comes pretty close what many call ‘spaghetti sauce’. Fry your cleaned livers together with some garlic in olive oil. Add white wine and let it evaporate before adding your chopped up peeled tomatoes. No need for excessive cooking. You could use fish instead of meat to make sauce. A tuna ragù for example. Or use legumes instead of meat. Healthy and tasty. Or go berserk and combine fish and legumes, as here where chickpeas and cod star.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the recipe for spaghetti aglio olio?
Answer: Spaghetti aglio olio (and chili pepper) is supposed to be a simple dish, often prepared when there is little time or desire for cooking. There are as many recipes as people preparing it, to their likes. Lately Italian chefs have been coming up with their take on this dish; nothing wrong with this but it feels like having parachutes designed by Dolce e Gabbana; simply superfluous. Anyway, use good olive oil, chili pepper, fresh garlic and parsley. And add a ladle of cooking water in order to obtain creaminess.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What do chefs typically do with leftover ingredients? Do they incorporate them into new dishes or throw them away?
Answer: When you see ‘chef’s surprise’ on a menu, you can bet it is a way to get rid of leftover ingredients. There is no time in a restaurant to get improvising as a well trained restaurant kitchen staff is trained to prepare dishes featuring on the menu, in the shortest time possible. Furthermore, it is not up to the chef to decide the quantity of ingredients to be purchased, that is work for the manager. Sometimes leftovers are given to the staff but usually they are, alas, binned. So one could conclude that ordering a ‘chef’s surprise’ is a noble act, saving ingredients from that somber destiny.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are the funniest, silliest, or rudest names for foods and dishes?
Answer: I can’t help but smiling every time I order them here in Palermo, Italy: cazzilli They also come as crocché (from the French croquet) but cazzilli is way funnier as it translates as little dicks. And that is exactly what they look like. Cazzilli often come with panelle, fried slabs of chickpea dough. In a sandwich. Life doesn’t get much better than that.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can raw olive oil be safely consumed on bread or crackers without heating it up first?
Answer: It is highly recommended to use raw oil for this purpose. It is actually very tasty. This is how the new oil is ‘tested’ after the harvest. Back in the city people have the first raw olive oil on muffulette; Fresh bread, a generous splash of oil, anchovy and pecorino cheese. Anyway, if you want to use olive oil, try to have it raw.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it common for people to eat pasta with butter?
Answer: Pasta with butter is a pretty established dish in Italy. Though it only contains three ingredients -pasta, butter and parmigiano cheese - the preparation requires some skill and consideration. First of all, the butter should not be heated/melted; take it out the fridge before you start cooking and cut it in little pieces. Your fresh boiled pasta -long pasta- is added to the butter with some of the water your pasta boiled in. Only then the parmigiano goes in. Mix thoroughly. It can be served with some more cheese on top. Serve the dish straight away as in very little time the butter solidifies and your pasta will stick together. The difference between soothing comfort food and a brick is only set seconds apart.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do I know if the olive oil I'm buying is truly organic?
Answer: That is, alas, almost impossible. European legislation doesn’t help as neither ‘organic’ nor ‘olive oil’ is truly defined. This means that olives have been cultivated without chemical-synthetic fertilisers, plant protection products, and soil herbicides. Many honest producers indeed keep to these rules but as there is little or no control on the territory, the ‘organic’ label is often obtained in order to sell (non organic) oil at higher prices. Furthermore, big producers buy their olives -and even oil- abroad, so control is virtually impossible. Anyway, finding the label on your bottle of olive oil is a good indicator, but not an absolute guarantee. The best olive oil, extra vergine oil, is obtained by cold pressing olives. The yielding (olives to olive oil) can’t exceed 20%. So 100 kg of olives will give you 20 litres of oil. And when done properly, this is indeed liquid gold. Perpetrators cut this oil with inferior oil, selling it as the original one. Again, the European legislation leaves too much room for malpractice, principally because controlling is hardly possible, probably due to powerful lobbying. Approach olive oil as you would approach fine wines. Do some tasting, read about it, inform yourself. Learn who produces the oil. And be prepared to pay the right price, understanding that quality doesn’t come cheap.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How does adding tomato to vegetable broth affect its taste?
Answer: Tomato, tomato paste to be more precise, can give your broth a deeper and more intense taste. A similar effect can be obtained by adding mushrooms. After roughly cutting up your vegetables -carrot, celery, onion - mix them up with a spoon of tomato paste before oven roast them. You want your vegetable to brown, not to burn. And make sure to get the juices from the bottom of your tray in the pot where these vegetables will then boil. I prefer to add the herbs -thyme, bay leaves, sage - after the vegetables come out of the oven as they tend to burn easily and leave a bitter taste.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Why is beef bouillon so salty?
Answer: Beef bouillon should not be salty; it becomes salty when salt is added before letting it reduce. Therefore, add some salt to the finished product, not before. There is no quick way to make a good stock. It is a long process thought most of the time it is just waiting, leaving you time to do whatever you please. Take that extra time to prepare a demi glace as it can be easily be frozen. My two cents: avoid them infamous factory made cubes and get cooking.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the typical dinner time in Italian homes? When is the best time to make a dinner appointment to avoid being too early or too late?
Answer: From personal experience, the more south one travels in Italy, the later people have dinner. In Sicily the earliest people have dinner is around eight. And when that dinner is less informal, even later. In summer time having dinner at nine thirty is not exceptional. So if you are not used to that, better have a snack in the late afternoon.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you suggest a simple and traditional Sicilian pasta dish?
Answer: One of the tastiest and yet easiest dishes in the Sicilian culinary landscape is pasta with breadcrumbs, locally known as pasta pasta ca muddica atturata. Heat some olive oil and add your breadcrumb, letting it turn golden brown. This is then set aside. In another pan heat some olive oil, a clove of garlic and some anchovy fillets. As soon as the latter disintegrate, add your fresh boiled pasta and mix. The whole is topped off with breadcrumb. Some notes; more than using store bought breadcrumb, make your own. It is a nice and respectful way to give bread an afterlife. And ideally, use the inside of the bread, not the crust. You can add some fresh chopped parsley or if you are lucky to have some, wild fennel. This dish is ‘classically’ make with bucatini, the hollow spaghetti like pasta, but normal spaghetti does the trick just fine.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What Korean food do you really like?
Answer: I’d go so far as stating that life without kimchi is not worth living it. Human life is divided in two parts, BK and AK, before and after kimchi. Twice a year, with my kids, we prepare a batch just to be sure we never run out. With few exceptions store bought kimchi is but a joke.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How can you determine if your risotto has too much liquid? What steps can you take to fix it?
Answer: I’m afraid it is too late to fix it once your rice is cooked. There are two main schools on making risotto; they both start by roasting the rice in a flat pot, together with some finely chopped onion. Then some white wine goes in. The first school then adds all the liquid at once and let the rice simmer away, sporadically stirring. When the rice absorbs all the liquid, your risotto is ready. The other school adds the liquid little by little and basically never stop stirring. You stop adding water when your rice is cooked. Thought there is no notable difference in taste and the first method is way easier, I’m kinda stuck in second school, enjoying the stirring and adding broth. And if you are not really sure how much water your should add, better join the second school, so you don’t end up with a soup rather than risotto.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can white chocolate be used in curry?
Answer: I am aware to be on thin ice here, as the information comes from an English friend who studied in Japan, years ago. Since I liked the story and it doesn’t seem all that unlikely, here we go. Japanese curry, when prepared at home, is made with store-bought roux and in order to give it a personal touch, people add their own special ingredients. My friend’s girlfriend would add some instant coffee, so he said, to make a killer-curry. Then the idea of adding white chocolate, which indeed pairs well with strong tasting food, might be possible.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What vegetables do you put in a beef stew?
Answer: Thank you for this question Margaret. I like to add carrots, onion and potatoes to my spezzatino, Italian beef stew. As they cook for quite some time, especially the potatoes and carrots keep intact. After serving the stew, what remains attached to the bottom is used to prepare pasta the following day. We call this glassa or glassa (from the French déglasser) It is one of the pasta dishes made with left overs. You either have this at home or in the authentic trattorias in the city of Palermo. An absolute must when you’re ever around.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What's the most unforgettable food that you have eaten in a foreign country?
Answer: The most vivid food related memory abroad dates back to early two thousands, in Northern Latvia. A holiday with a goal, visiting a friend who was then writing and working on the restoration of mansion that had been burned a few years earlier. After some days in the capital Riga my kids were going berserk; it was summer and they wouldn’t sleep till it got dark, basically never. Apart from drunk tourists it was a fine city. The food was on the interesting side, nothing spectacular though. It was driving up north in a rental car, kids singing in the back, we got lost trying an alternative way to reach the Gauja national park. So I stopped the car by a lonely farm in the middle of nowhere, asking for directions. The man working in his garden didn’t understand a word I was saying, my fault, but after having spotted the kids, ushered us in, as if he had been waiting for us to arrive. While I showed him my map -and he scratched the back of his head - his wife took care of my wife and children, offering them biscuits and juice. The fact that our conversation was based on gesturing and guessing made the situation unreal but not altogether unpleasant. When he stood up, I stood up and followed him around the small farm. In a stable I saw my children happily stroking a horse, talking to my new met friend’s wife, in a language no one but them understood. We walked and he showed me a barn like construction where fish was hanging to smoke. Once back in the farm house the table was laid. The food was genuine and nice, the smoked fish heavenly. My kids just kept on eating and the farmer’s wife kept on feeding them. It wasn’t easy to get back in the car as my kids and the farmer’s wife kept hugging. The farmer drove ahead leading us to a crossroad. I got out of the car to thank him once more and received carefully pack smoked fish. From then on we ordered smoked fish wherever we ate, but nothing came even close to what we had that day. Or as my children said, the one that auntie (la zietta) makes.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What inexpensive fish could I buy in lieu of tuna?
Answer: In Sicily the tuna season is short but fortunately we have alalunga, albacore (Thunnus alalunga) It is also know as ‘white tuna’ is smaller and is milder in taste. As it is fished all year round, it costs less then tuna. It ain’t exactly inexpensive but still cheaper than tuna.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the process for removing water from cooked canned tomatoes?
Answer: A fresh tomato is made up of about 95% of water. Canned tomatoes roughly the same. The easiest -and frankly the only one I can think of - way to reduce the water content is by heating them in an uncovered pan. Give them an occasionally stir as the water evaporates.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What strange kinds of meat have you tried?
Answer: It happened to have kinds of meat that were strange to me but pretty random where they were served. Cuy, guinea pig, in Peru. Camel meat in Morocco Porcupine in Vietnam -and Canada But the weirdest of them all is the ubiquitous meat served in fast food joints.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can spaghetti be made with only tomato-based pasta sauces and no meat? If so, what is your favorite recipe or brand that is free of animal products?
Answer: Sure you can, actually the adding of meat - in Italy- to tomato sauce is an exception rather than a rule. There are various ways to prepare yourself a lovely plate of spaghetti using mainly tomatoes. Leave the jars at the supermarket and prepare it yourself. This is probably the most Italian dish, as it is eaten from North to South, from East to West. There is no precise recipe but it all boils down to seasoning fresh boiled spaghetti with ‘passata’. A nice way is to fry a clove of garlic in olive oil, add your passata and let it boil for ten minutes. Fresh boiled spaghetti are added and thoroughly stirred. A generous adding of grated cheese and you’re ready. Pretty similar to the latter dish, but instead of passata you use peeled and diced tomatoes. They come ready canned but it ain’t so difficult peeling them yourself, using fresh tomatoes. Just cut your tomatoes in half, fry them in olive oil and add your spaghetti. Cherry tomatoes don’t have to be peeled, so it’s quick and easy to prepare. A tad more difficult but well worth the effort. Peel your tomatoes and mix them with almonds, basil, garlic and olive oil. All raw. Let it rest for a couple of hours and then mix it with your pasta. A winner.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it recommended to drain off the oil before eating canned tuna?
Answer: Yes, you should get rid of that oil, even when it says that is olive oil. In origin boiled tuna was topped off with olive oil in order to conserve it. The remaining oil was used to season dishes containing that same tuna, but since these jars are boiled, the oil loses most of its taste and properties. Canned tuna uses inferior oil, only to remind people of the traditional recipe. Just drain it.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What food or drink did you consume to reduce anxiety after a tough day?
Answer: During the week this rarely happens but on Friday evenings the end of the week is often marked by a couple of cocktails and simple snacks; crisps, olives, bread and oil. One cocktail reduces the accumulated stress, the second eliminates it. A third one would jeopardise the Saturday morning. As Dorothy Parker taught: I like to have a martini, Two at the very most. After three I’m under the table, after four I’m under my host

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What's your favorite healthy ingredient to use in cooking?
Answer: No doubt about that: our own olive oil. We use it especially in salads and to top pasta off with. Health and taste combined. Tomato salad wouldn’t be half as tasty without. Though I admit that adding it to pasta is an act of gluttony more than anything else.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the purpose of salting eggplant before cooking? How does salting the flesh affect the texture and flavor of the eggplant after it is cooked?
Answer: It is a common use to sprinkle some salt on cut eggplant as it removes the bitterness. The salt, together with the bitter liquid is then removed, leaving the eggplant with pretty much the same texture. There is a little trick here, one that greengrocers don’t like. When buying eggplant, you should look for ‘male’ ones, as they contain less seeds and are less bitter. How do you distinguish a ‘male’ from a ‘female’ eggplant? Quite simple: Look at the bottom and and you’ll see that he female eggplant has a long brownish slit-like indentation at the bottom. The male’s marking is more round. I wish I’d be able to come up with an mnemonic to help you remembering…

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is a dish made of tuna and noodles considered healthy?
Answer: Sure it is. Even if tuna is indeed more likely to contain more lead than other (smaller) fish. And though lead is seriously unhealthy, it’s not just lead it contains. It is rich in protein and contains many vitamins and minerals such as B-Complex vitamins, Vitamins A and D as well as iron, selenium and phosphorus. Even the canned tuna. So please enjoy your nice pasta al tonno. Canned or fresh

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is fagottini pasta?
Answer: Fagotto is the Italian for bundle and has no negative connotation as it does in English. Fresh pasta is wrapped around the filling of your choice. They can be baked, boiled or steamed.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is buying pasta by weight still a common practice in Italy?
Answer: Pasta fresca is still sold by weight, in specialised shops. As Massimo Saracino already pointed out, dried pasta is usually sold by the kilo in supermarkets. Mind you that fresh pasta is rather expensive.; if often goes for ten times the price of dried pasta.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the recipe for Italian veal scallopini?
Answer: Scallopini is a way of cutting meat; very thin in this case. These slices are then passed through flour and briefly fried. Usually a liquid is added which will thicken because of the flour. Some favourites… Marsala is a rather sweet Sicilian wine you ought to have hanging around in the kitchen. Zibbibbo, a tad sweeter still, is a good alternative.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the best way to serve homemade pizza at a party buffet style?
Answer: Pizza is good whether piping hot or stone cold. As most people prefer the first, you could organise a girapizza: fresh baked pizza is sliced up and distributed. Continue to bake pizzas till people are satisfied. It is also a nice way to get some variety.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some suggestions for broccoli and pasta?
Answer: If you have the opportunity, buy your broccoli like this: Use the leaves and the stalk as it gives you more flavour. Anyway, here are two nice ways to use broccoli when making pasta. Steam or boil your broccoli. If you boil them, use the same water to boil your pasta in. Fry a clove of garlic in olive oil and add some anchovy fillets. Sauté your broccoli and add fresh boiled pasta. Fast, easy and very tasty indeed. Blend steamed or boiled broccoli with some olive oil, grated parmigiano and seasoning. If you have any nuts laying around, add them. Mix the cream with fresh boiled pasta. You could enrich this dish with fried bacon.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is Parmigiano Reggiano cheese typically served on top of risotto in Italy? Is this a common way of eating risotto outside of Italy as well?
Answer: Risotto does not come with parmigiano on top, the cheese is added at the end of the preparation, with the heat off. Adding more cheese at the table, once the risotto is served, is an uncouth act, saying what has being served doesn’t pleased you.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some reasons why some people may not like risotto?
Answer: The dislike may derive from the aspect risotto typically has; it seems mushy yet that is actually the way it is supposed to look. Whereas other rice preparation are preceded by washing rice in order to get rid of some of the starch in order to obtain separate grains after boiling it, risotto thrives on starch hence the ‘gluey’ aspect. It’s not a good reason to dislike risotto, but a reason altogether.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do you cook pastina?
Answer: Pastina ought to be cooked in broth. Add some fresh grated parmigiano cheese and you have Italian comfort food by excellence.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you recommend any good recipes for sweet and sour cucumber salad?
Answer: I can’t frankly remember the origin of this dish but little does that matter. It is easy to prepare. Sprinkle sliced (or cubed if you please) cucumber with salt and let it rest for half an hour. Remove the liquid, add sugar, vinegar and chili pepper. Dried chili pepper does fine but sambal really gives it a kick.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What types of cheese should not be used for cooking?
Answer: Processed cheese -is that even cheese?- should be avoided. It can turn a reasonably good dish in smut. Or a terrible dish in abhorrence A close second place goes to grated parmesan in a can You’re worth more than that, really.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Why is Michelle Obama so dumb? She forced us to eat healthier. Eating unhealthy is healthier than eating nothing. We shouldn’t prevent kids to drink chocolate mild, eat burgers, & force them to go vegan. We should have the right to eta what we want.
Answer: Why all that bitterness? As a public figure Michelle Obama advocated healthy food, she never forced anyone, as far as I know. Being the wife of a president she could deal with so-called minor causes. That’s what first-ladies do. “I’m a big believer in healthy eating because it reflects on your mind and your body,” said Melania Trump, surrounded by about a dozen children in the garden on Friday afternoon. “I encourage you to continue to eat a lot of vegetables and fruits, so you grow up healthy and take care of yourself.” Melania Trump in Politico. The last thing I want to do here is to polarise. It is just very difficult to be against healthy food. Obesity, coronary diseases and diabetes are a direct result of unhealthy eating. And sure, you can’t force people not to eat unhealthy food, you are right, but one may show an alternative. When the choice is between unhealthy food or dying of hunger, well, then indeed it takes leading figures to step in and offer an alternative.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some alternative ways to prepare butternut squash besides making it into a soup or mash?
Answer: Though usually prepared with pumpkin, the butternut squash version works pretty well, too. Peel and slice the squash; fry the slabs in olive oil with (unpeeled) garlic. When cooked through season with salt, add a mixture of sugar and vinegar and some fresh mint leaves.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you recommend a budget-friendly brand for spaghetti noodles?
Answer: It believe this is a false problem. You get what you pay for: very cheap pasta is usually of dubious quality whereas more expensive pasta is usually high in quality. This being said, you are going to need about one hundred grams per person (3.5oz). Even more expensive pasta, say 8 euro (dollar) a kilo will set you only 80 cents back.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the best way to store leftover uncooked dry pasta for future use?
Answer: Put it in an airtight container and don’t store it for too long. Pasta may contain the eggs of the Plodia interpunctella, especially the more expensive kinds of pasta as they are slow dried with temperatures that don’t eliminate kill the eggs. When kept for too long, the eggs may metamorphose in larvae and in a next stage in little insects. Nothing to worry about, the eggs are not dangerous to humans. Neither are the larvae and insects but just bin that pasta.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some simple and tasty recipes for cooking and eating green beans?
Answer: A personal favourite, insalata vastasa. Vastasa is Sicilian for rowdy, uncouth, loutish; not exactly a flattering name. It could derive from the fact that all the ingredients can bought in the same place, a (Sicilian) greengrocer. Apart from fresh vegetables they sell boil potatoes and boiled green beans (in summer). So all you do is mix the ingredients together and serve. This might be considered a short-cut and hence kinda cheating. Anyway, apart from boiled green beans and potatoes it contains raw onion, tomato and olives. The salad is seasoned with vinegar, olive oil and an abundant dusting of oregano. When preparing the dish at home, have mercy when boiling the green beans, leave some bite to them.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some recipes that use gorgonzola cheese?
Answer: For Easter many Sicilian ‘expats’ come home to spend the holiday with their family. So did my dear friend Alessandro who teaches at the Politecnico in Milano. As you can no longer bring cheese on board of a plane, he jeopardised his intere luggage with a block of artisanal gorgonzola cheese. Anyway, so far we had a wonderful risotto with gorgonzola, pears and walnuts and pasta with gorgonzola and radicchio In both dishes the cheese is added right at the end, just giving it the time to melt. At this rate we’ll be out of gorgonzola by next week (I ate quite a bit, on bread, coming home late yesterday night) and the countdown to the next academic recess already started.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: I want to use lentils and make burgers. What do you recommend to be an easy recipe?
Answer: As Terry Dinerman already and rightfully pointed out, don’t food yourself. That being said, lentil patties are bliss. You can prepare them with leftover lentils. Just mix them with some grated cheese and breadcrumb. Roll balls and flatten them. As the lentils are already seasoned, there is no need for other seasoning.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you suggest some traditional Portuguese dishes that can be made at home?
Answer: A very hearty soup and easy to make dish is caldo verde, green soup. Though in Portugal people use couve Galega, you could use kale or other kinds of leafy cabbage. Anyway, after frying onion and garlic in oil, potatoes and (watered down) broth is added. Once soft, let the soup cool down a bit and blend before adding the finely sliced cabbage and bring it back to a boil. Tradition goes that each gets one slice of chorizo

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Do Italians commonly put cold cuts on pizza? If yes, what types of cold cuts are typically used?
Answer: Cold cuts are pretty standard in Italian pizzerias. Finely sliced raw ham is added once the pizza is baked. Together with some shaved parmigiano and rocket. This pizza often comes as San Daniele. Another by now classic on the Italian pizza menu, a four season pizza, quattro stagioni. Ham and olive represent winter. Artichokes represent spring, mushrooms autumn, tomato and basil summer. Or on what over here is known as pizza romana, with just mozzarella and ham It comes standard on some pizzas such as Diavola but can be added to other pizzas as well. Bresaola, air cured beef, is added after the pizza is baked in much the same way as raw ham. Speck on the other hand is usually added before baking or half way through.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Should the Bay leaf be removed from spaghetti sauce before serving?
Answer: As you don’t actually eat a bay leave, and it doesn’t even look good, it is better to remove the leaves.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you suggest a simple dish that includes tomatoes (excluding pizza)?
Answer: A personal summer salad Tomato and red onion, a drizzle of olive oil and pinch of salt. If you want and have time, sprinkle some salt over the onion and let it rest for an hour then rinse before adding it to the salad. Don’t forget to serve it with bread to mop up the juice. Basil is an optional.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the reason for the popularity of cannoli in America, considering their origin in Italy?
Answer: Apart from being tasty there might be other reasons. Millions of Sicilians migrated to the United states and passed their culinary tradition on. Among these the emblematic sweet, related to festivities. Cannoli are furthermore not as complicated to prepare as the other Sicilian sweet, a cassata cake.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is veggie pizza, Italian?
Answer: This is a very interesting question indeed. If veggie stands for vegetarian it should be pointed out that the denomination veggie or vegetarian comes much later than the conception of pizzas. In Italy and in other parts of the world dishes that not contained meat or fish weren’t featured as vegetarian but simple as food. This delight is a pizza margherita, and though it contains no meat, calling it a vegetarian pizza is probably a bridge too far. Whether pizza with veggies originates in Italy, I don’t know. It exists alright, and often comes as ortolana, greengrocer pizza.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How can homemade pistachio paste be served in the most delicious way?
Answer: Not the lightest of pasta dishes but very tasty indeed. After having fried cubed pancetta -or bacon if you please with a clove of garlic, remove the garlic and ricotta cheese and pistachio paste. Add your fresh boiled pasta and some of the water it boiled in to the mixture. Mix thoroughly and serve piping hot.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: I know someone who lives in a shelter. Several meals a week are only veggies and pasta/rice. Is this a sustainable diet?
Answer: More than sustainable, that seems a pretty healthy diet. When legumes -notably cheap- are added, this would come very close to the original Mediterranean diet.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the standard serving size for spaghetti? Can this information be found online?
Answer: There is no such a thing as a universal standard serving. As there is no standard serving of sandwiches, potatoes or rice. In Italy people boil about one hundred grams per person (3.5oz). Where this satisfies Italians, there is a general tendency to increase that number.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do I make fish finger at home?
Answer: Fish fingers were ‘invented’ to use up discarded fish, trimmings and other unsellable parts. Anyway, you can coat white fish with breadcrumbs and fry. The coating helps to keep your fish from becoming dry. There are different ways of coating the fish. The easiest is to pass your fish in oil before breading. This will conserve the taste but results less crunchy. The swordfish can be cut in strips, it doesn’t have to be a whole slice as in the picture. Or pass the fish in flour first, then in beaten eggs before breading. It is crunchier but the egg compromised the taste of fish. What will resemble store-bought fish fingers best is when you batter the fish before breading.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it possible to use olive oil instead of vegetable oil when making homemade mayonnaise?
Answer: You will end up with an emulsion alright, but taste-wise it is disaster. Furthermore, good olive oil is pretty expensive and you need a lot of oil to prepare mayonnaise. If you do it for health reasons, preparing mayonnaise is probably not the wisest idea.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do I make homemade cannolis at home?
Answer: Cannoli (which is already the plural of cannolo, so no need for the ‘s’) are usually store bought since they require quite some work. Especially the crust is troublesome to prepare. The dough is made with flour, lard, eggs, cinnamon, marsala wine, salt and orange zest. After rolling the dough out, slabs are modelled around a metal cylinder and deep fried. Often the dough sticks to the metal cylinder and burning your fingers is almost inevitable. Anyway, after letting the shells cool down they are filled with a ricotta, chocolate and sugar mix and topped off with candied fruit. See why most people don’t mind going to the pastry shop and buying them?

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How can fried eggplants be made less greasy?
Answer: Eggplant is very sponge-like. If you fry them, they absorb oil and even when placed on paper towels, one doesn’t get rid of all the oil. So if you please to have your eggplant not greasy, don’t use oil. You could grill or oven bake them and then add the wanted amount of olive oil later.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is pasta good for babies?
Answer: Sure, that’s what most Italians babies are fed. Well, rather than pasta, pastina (little pasta) is used. Mixed with vegetable puree or jarred baby food.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you explain the difference between caponata and eggplant parmigiana?
Answer: They are two different dishes, both with Sicilian origins. Eggplant grows profusely in Sicily and ripens in summer, hence the countless recipes involving this vegetable in the area. A classic in the Sicilian culinary scene, though recipes differ from door to door. It all comes down to cook (boil or fry) onion, celery and eggplant with the adding of capers, olives and tomato sauce. Being a sweet sour dish, some sugar and vinegar are added. Caponata is served as a starter, served with bread in order to mop up the juice. There are countless variations featuring ingredients ranging from apples to swordfish. Here the eggplant is sliced before being fried. Don’t oven bake them as you’ll break the hearts of many Sicilian cooks. Anyway, fried eggplant slices are layered with fresh made tomato sauce, grated cheese (pecorino or caciocavallo) and basil leaves. This dish too is eaten cold, and served with bread. Summer at its best.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it common for people to put butter on Italian food? Is this a traditional way of eating in Italy?
Answer: In the past more than now butter was an exotic ingredient in southern Italy. Due to the climate milk was drunk straight away or turned in cheese. Butter and cream don’t thrive in a hot weather. But as it goes with exotic product, they are valued higher than local ones. So adding some butter to fresh boiled pasta was considered a restorative dish, often feed to people recovering from illnesses. Topped off with grated cheese it now, even in the south, a pretty popular dish.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do I make eggplant parmigiana?
Answer: I can tell you how this dish is prepared in Sicily. And people over here will tell you this is the only way to prepare parmigiana. When Sicilians make parmigana, there is no parmigiano cheese involved. The name refers to the wooden shutters, called parmiciane, as they resemble the layered form of the dish. After sprinkling salt on sliced eggplant slices and letting them ‘sweat’ out some of the bitter liquid, the contain, the slabs are dried and fried. In the meantime prepare a tomato sauce. Fry an onion, add tomato sauce and let it bubble away for at least half an hour. From there on it is all very easy: layer the fried eggplant, sauce and grated cheese. As told before, this cheese isn’t parmigiano but rather pecorino or caciocavallo. Instead of baking this delight, it is placed in the fridge and eaten cold.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it true that Italians have reduced their consumption of pasta due to concerns about childhood obesity? If not, what may be the reason for this misconception?
Answer: It is a misconception alright; recently food pundits have been preaching against carbs, blaming them for weight-gainers and obesity. And yes, they even convinced some Italians to renounce having pasta. Overall, innately, Italians know how much pasta they can eat and accompany this with vegetables and the right amount of proteine. The increase of child obesity in Italy is due to other product. Soft drinks, processed food, cereals, snacks. Not because they have pasta for lunch. Not in the past, not now and not in the future.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some popular Italian cuisine procedures?
Answer: Although it has its origin in Northern Italy, mantecare is now nation-wide procedure. Mantecare, derives from the Spanish word for butter, refers to the adding of oil or butter at the end of the procedure, in order to make dish creamy. A classic example is baccalà mantecato The same procedure can be found when making risotto. Right at the end of the preparation, with the heat off, butter and cheese is added. That last stirring will result in creamy risotto. Or with pasta. Add your fresh boiled pasta to the condiment, together with some water it boiled in and a drizzle of oil. Again, you’ll obtain that creamy result.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How do I make farfalle pasta taste good? What is the best sauce to use?
Answer: There are two dishes that actually require farfalle pasta in Italy. And both have their roots in the decade of decadenze, the eighties. Fry a finely chopped shallot in butter, add cut up salmon and a shot of vodka. Then the cream goes in followed by fresh cooked farfalle. Usually made with frozen peas. Can’t say it ain’t tasty neither that it is a great dish. For many it’s a trip down memory lane.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Do canned lentils need to be soaked before cooking, even if they are pre-soaked?
Answer: No need soaking canned lentils but a nice thorough rinsing is recommended. Canned lentils contain a lot of salt - sodium. 230 Some of it washed off under running water. And just by the way, neither dried lentils need soaking.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it considered offensive to ask for ketchup with pizza or spaghetti Bolognese at a restaurant in Italy?
Answer: It would be considered a provocation rather than an offence, and might trigger the waiter’s eyebrows to raise or his eyes to roll. The thing is that restaurants in Italy do not have ketchup. Pizzerias who offer chips as starter -that is a real thing in Italy - instead usually have sachets that come with those chips. I guess you could ask for some to go along with your pizza. Again, you may be frowned upon but not denied to do so. Be quick though because those sachets are about to disappear soon due to European regulation.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is spaghetti with pesto a tasty dish? Can cream or other ingredients be added to make a creamy pesto sauce?
Answer: Adding cream to pesto in order to make it creamy is a crying shame. It ruins the delicate mixture at once. The creaminess is obtained by adding some of the water your pasta boiled in and mix thoroughly. Pasta with pesto is a tasty dish that needs no adding of any kind. Not even cherry tomatoes Just enjoy the balance between basil, pine nuts olive oil, cheese and olive oil.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some ways to make non-tomato based sauces for pasta from scratch in Italian cuisine?
Answer: There are a myriad of ways to prepare non-tomato based sauces or condiments. Many recipes start with frying garlic in olive oil. As soon as the garlic releases its fragrance, the garlic is removed. With the adding of some chili pepper and parsley you end up with pasta aglio e olio. This can be enriched with many ingredients, ranging from bottarga (dried fish roe) to vegetables. It is of utter importance to add your pasta to this condiment and not vice versa. A personal favourite is to blend slightly boiled (or steamed) vegetables together with olive oil and grated cheese. You can use almost all vegetables. In the picture the vegetables in question are zucchini Then there is the minestrone category. Varies veggies are boiled and pasta is added. No need for tomatoes. Even the ubiquitous Bolognese has a tomato-less variant: ragù in bianco

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What’s on the menu for Easter?
Answer: It’s all very promising. First of all, we’ll be guests at a friend’s house near the sea. The weather forecast says -promises- we’ll have a swim. Food-wise things are even better. As my friend’s mom is from Apulia and invited quite some relatives, they’ll be loaded with local specialities. Which triggers a ‘food-war’. The Sicilians are not going to sit idle and simply accept this bonanza. Apart from the obligatory roasted lamb, the barbecue will have no rest. As for sweets, I just ordered four cassata cakes. As to continue in war terminology, these will be our nukes… Happy Easter to you all.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Are imported ingredients cheaper to cook with than local ones?
Answer: Alas, this sometimes happen. In Sicily, where I live, imported lentils are cheaper than locally grown ones. The same goes for wheat. The majority of the lentils found in Sicily -and Italy- are Canadian. They cultivate large flat fields and as it goes when growing single crops, use quite a bit of pesticides. The cultivation is heavily machine-based; from planting, spraying to harvesting. Even when travelling all the way to Europe, they remain cheaper than local grown ones. Whereas Sicilian lentil fields are smaller and more manually-based, making them more expensive. What really strikes me is the fact that Canadians hardly eat any lentils; over 99% of the lentils are exported.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the quintessential Mediterranean dish?
Answer: One dish, spread all over the Mediterranean, overclasses all concurrence. A bowl of piping hot lentil soup. It is quintessential as it contains ingredients that are readily found and further more, are affordable. Stewed legumes and vegetables have been eaten and savoured for thousands of years in the Mediterranean area; even the bible mentions this dish, when Esau swaps his birthright for a nice plate of lentil stew. Fry some onion and garlic in olive oil, add your cut up vegetables (carrot and celery) and washed lentils. Cover with water and let it bubble away. Top it off with a drizzle of olive oil.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the recipe for anchovy sauce?
Answer: I would strongly dissuade you from doing this at home. Not only does it require a shipload of anchovy, the smell isn’t all that pleasant. Anchovies are layered and topped off with salt in a slotted wooden bucket. Over time the sauce drips out. In Italy this is known as colatura di alice and is akin with fish sauce and garum. A wonderful product that gives an umami boost to many recipes.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it possible to make too much pasta for a meal?
Answer: Sure it is possibile, actually, in some cases it is recommendable. The average Italian portion is about 100g per person (3.5oz) but now and then they throw in some more, not to increase the portions but to set aside. This pasta can be fried in olive oil -or butter if you please - with a generous adding of grated cheese. Of utter importance is to get some crust. There are some limits to this practice: only left over pasta can be fried, it has to sit in the fridge for at least one day. You furthermore need a pasta that is not too heavily seasoned. Ideally pasta with tomato sauce is used. And lastly, set the pasta aside before you start eating, as the temptation to have more pasta is always lurking.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Why do you use Parmesan cheese?
Answer: There is always a wedge of Parmesan sitting in the fridge We grate it over pasta or cut of a small piece when we want a snack. Though it is far from the only cheese we buy, it’s the one that is perennially present. Why? Because it is terribly tasty and versatile.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some recommended side dishes to serve with oven fried fish?
Answer: A simple fennel salad goes well with oven baked fish. A drizzle of olive oil, some black pepper and a pinch of salt. Highly recommendable as it cleans your palate and enhances the taste of fish.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it possible to overcook canned tuna?
Answer: Yes, tuna is pretty similar to beef regarding cooking time. No cooking time whatsoever when preparing sashimi or tuna tartare. A quick searing when eaten as a steak. Overcooking here results in a stringy, unpleasant dish. Not as long as a meat ragù, tuna may simmer for quite a while when prepared as such. Not more than half an hour as it would lose all its taste.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What happens when fish is overcooked?
Answer: It doesn’t taste like much anymore which doesn’t mean it becomes inedible. In the Caribbean area they often deep-fry the hell out of fish, leaving only the meat close to the bone remains somehow soft. Though surely not the best way to prepare fish, it brings back nice memories.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some edible flowers, and how are they used in culinary dishes?
Answer: Edible flowers - there’s quite a lot of them - are often used in upscale restaurants. As these places are bound to strict rules, they buy them from growers, and they don’t come cheap. Though they have a specific taste, flowers are usually added to embellish dishes. There are some more main-stream flowers that are easier to obtain. Zucchini flowers are pretty popular in Italy. They are stuffed with mozzarella cheese and anchovies, battered and fried. Truth be told, the flower ain’t much more than a vessel. More interesting are proto flowers or buds. Among them are artichokes and capers. They are picked before they blossom. While figs are actually inverted flowers

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some recommended methods for cooking artichoke hearts? Is it necessary to cook them, or can they be eaten raw and still be enjoyable?
Answer: When using fresh artichokes, is to work thoroughly, not minding the waste. Cut to top off and remove the outer leaves till reaching the tender ones. Peel the stalk and remove the fluffy part inside. Make sure to wear rubber gloves; some artichokes have nasty spines and more in general because they stain your hands terribly. Once you have your hearts, fun starts. You can indeed have them raw. It is of utter importance to bathe the finely sliced hearts in water and lemon to avoid oxidation. You can blanch your hearts and use them in a variety of recipes. They can be added to pies, salads, pasta or just served as such. A personal favourite is turning them in a cream; blended with a clove of garlic, olive oil and some grated cheese. This can be used as a spread, filling for a pie or served with pasta.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some places in Sicily, Italy that one must visit while traveling there by car?
Answer: Leave the main road and wonder around, get lost -you will, even if you try not to, due to lame signage. Have a coffee in a bar, try some of the local food, appreciate the nothing-to-do-nor-see experience. Ask if someone sells fresh ricotta or cheese. Enjoy being hold up by a passing herd of sheep. Embrace the bucolic setting and forgot your worries.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some quick and easy recipes for homemade pasta dishes?
Answer: In Italy quick pasta dishes are those where the making of the condiment/sauce is shorter or the same than the boiling your pasta. Most daily pastas make part of that category. Not only is this a fast way of preparing food, the reduced cooking time for your vegetables -yes, most daily pasta recipes are vegetable based - makes sure they keep a crunch, and taste. Just a couple of days ago we had pasta with green cauliflower. Cut in small florets they boiled together with the spaghetti. In the meantime we toasted some breadcrumb. The adding of pine nuts and raisins as an option, a very Sicilian one.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How many eggs can small fishes have?
Answer: Averagely they have 40,000 of them and they are contained in a sack. The smaller the fish, the smaller the eggs. and closer look: Fishmongers almost always put the eggs aside when cleaning fish, and if not specifically asked by the client, keep them for themselves. Very shrewd indeed because they are a true delight. When used in pasta, add them right at the end and by no means over-cook them; they should pop in your mouth when eating. As here, prepared with fried eggplant and cherry tomatoes. So next time at the fishmonger, ask for the eggs.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Who loves pasta with garlic toast?
Answer: I do When the toast is reduced to breadcrumb, fried in olive oil and garlic and goes on top of pasta. Count me out if you meant this:

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some recommended sauces for a fruit salad?
Answer: Some years ago I was asked to prepare a fruit salad for a kind of pot luck dinner. It bothered me greatly as a fruit salad ain’t but cut up fruit. So I cut all the different fruits in identical dice and build a cube. The picture below isn’t mine; the blocks I used were slightly bigger, and straighter. Doing so a lot of edges go to waste. You can blend these together with a hit of maraschino and use it as a sauce. Don’t forget to add a pinch of salt. A square meal ;-)

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Does ordering toppings on your pizza mean you get less cheese?
Answer: It is charming how Italian and American pizza ordering works, seemingly different but at the end of the day with the same result. By no means I want to generalise, so please take no offence if you had a different experience. Ordering toppings in a basic pizza is the American way. Italians have to chose from a menu, but can then ask for modifications. And these can be substantial. The very first time I went to a pizzeria I was afraid the waiter was going to freak out; no one ordered by telling what pizza from the list they wanted; all asked to remove, replace or add ingredients. In neither system the basic amount of cheese decreases by ordering extra topics.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is your favorite vehicle for using up leftovers?
Answer: Polpette… Most leftovers have a splendid afterlife when turned into polpette, balls. The principal is always the same: cut up the leftovers, mix them with an egg, breadcrumb and grated cheese, roll little balls and fry away. They are excellent as a starter or aperitif. Some examples. Polpette di carne, meatballs Broccoli Bread Lentils Salmon The list goes on and on; risotto, zucchini, eggplant, artichokes…

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are the characteristics of authentic Sicilian cuisine? Are there any variations in food preparation across different regions of Sicily?
Answer: There is such a thing as the Sicilian signature. When dishes contain pine nuts and raisins, they are very likely Sicilian. The raisins are only little bigger than a peppercorn and not all that sweet. They cannot be substituted with the dreaded big white ones. This mixture can be found in pasta dishes as well as in meat and fish dishes. Pasta with sardines Polpette di sarde, sardine balls

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Do you use anchovies in your cooking? If you do, what recipes and why?
Answer: In the Sicilian cuisine - and in other Italian regions - anchovies is often used to enhance the favour of a dish. When served, there won’t any anchovy to be spotted though. It is the first step for many delicious recipes; you heat some olive oil and fry garlic and some anchovy fillets till they fall apart. The easiest recipe is to add your pasta to this mixture and top it off with toasted breadcrumbs A tad more challenging is when green cauliflower, tomato paste, pine nuts and raisons are added. Well worth a try though.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the reason behind putting cheese on top of spaghetti instead of adding it to the sauce while making it from scratch?
Answer: The main reason is that not everybody wants cheese in or on their pasta. Putting cheese on pasta is done at the table, where everybody decides how much they want to add. Adding too much is considered loutish and covers all other tastes. There are some exceptions. In cacio e pepe and carbonara pasta the cheese goes in the condiment.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is your preferred sauce for spaghetti or pasta? What sets it apart from other sauces? Do you have a preference between red or white sauce?
Answer: I am very fond of aglio olio, garlic and oil. Especially of the enriched versions. It always start with frying a clove of garlic and a chili pepper in olive oil and ends with the adding of fresh chopped parsley. A squeeze of lemon and some zest to obtain this With a generous grating of bottarga, fish roe, and you end up with this delight And when having to celebrate, add sea urchin eggs What sets it apart from other sauces or condiments is the simplicity, the straightforwardness.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you suggest any variations or additions to the classic spinach and feta pizza recipe?
Answer: The Italian take on this combo is made with ricotta instead of feta cheese, and it’s a match made in heaven. The mixture is pretty versatile, used to fill ravioli, pies and season pasta. Steamed spinach is mixed with fresh ricotta and nutmeg.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is your favorite non-traditional pizza topping, other than pineapple?
Answer: A guilty-pleasure is pizza with kebab. It comes with a garlicky yogurt and hot sauce. It is an interesting intersection of two traditional dishes. Until not too long ago it was a rarity on the menu of pizzerie in Italy. Nowadays most of them serve them.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What does sea urchin taste like? How can you cook or prepare sea urchin?
Answer: Sea urchins are a true delicacy. Saying they taste like sea is a little reductive. Their saltiness is well balanced with sweetness. But only when they are not fully cooked, much like oysters. The easiest way to serve them is freshly opened, with a piece of bread to mop up the juice. Making pasta with sea urchins is pretty easy, once you get get the pulp (the eggs) out and removed all the spines. One single spine may ruin the whole dish. Fry a clove of garlic and a little chili pepper in olive oil. Turn off the heat, add you fresh boiled pasta and the urchins; it is an elaborated version of pasta with oil and garlic if you please. Some fresh chopped parsley and you’re ready to go.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it necessary to cook Prosciutto before consuming it, or can it be used as a topping without any additional cooking by the end user?
Answer: There are two kinds of prosciutto, at least in Italy. Cotto e crudo, boiled and raw. Both are ready to eat as they come. Actually, any further cooking decreases the value, especially when cooking with raw ham. For example, when used on pizza, it is added when the pizza comes out of the oven. Cotto on the other hand can be eaten as it comes but is often used in cooking. Two favourites: Pasta prosciutto, panna e piselli (PPPP) pasta with ham, cream and peas; pure comfort food Spuma di prosciutto

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Do Italian style pizzas typically have olives as a topping?
Answer: Some pizzas come with olives but it is not a condicio sine qua non. What is, imho, important is to add deboned olives. Few things are peskier than biting into an olive pit To eat without risking an emergency visit to the dentist you should eat the olives separately, ruining the pizza experience.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How can you incorporate more vegetables into your favorite pasta dishes?
Answer: Interesting question. Pasta with vegetables is pretty usually, at least in Italy. You can only add so many vegetables as pasta can carry. That is usually a fifty fifty ratio. If you please to add more vegetables, the best way is to blend them. With some olive oil and a drizzle of oil. Let’s take the example of pasta with artichokes; cut in pieces you add about one artichoke per portion Blending the artichokes you can serve two per person Some goes for most vegetables

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: When did Arancini become popular in Italy? Were they always considered a street food or were they traditionally served at home?
Answer: Arancini -or better still, arancine - are not real street food. They are prepared and sold by bars or prepared at home in Sicily. They were conceived by the Arabs when they conquered Sicily, as a way to eat goat meat covered by rice cooked with saffron. Today the filling is different but the idea remained: a whole meal you can hold in your hand. Though Sicilians migrated by the millions to Northern Italy, they had some kind of discretion regarding their food. They would prepare it alright but kept it to themselves in order not to be discriminated and labeled as terroni. The unbridled pride is a recent phenomenon, so it took a far too long for arancine to become popular.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you eat fish and eggs together? Is it harmful for health?
Answer: Just yesterday we had frittatine di merluzzo in a local eatery. Small cod omelets if you please. As a starter though listed as secondi. Feeling more than fine today. Can’t be bad.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is your favourite food and drink pairing?
Answer: Drinking water after eating artichokes is a bliss. Apparently the effect of eating artichokes is pretty devastating on our papilla. A glass of water will taste pleasant and sweet, while wine will taste twisted. Water is usually a good pairing with any food, but artichokes…is like a party in my mouth and everybody’s invited.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it true that most Italians take a spoonful of olive oil before they eat breakfast?
Answer: Surely not most Italians, but some do. It is believed to avoid tooth decay. Then again, other cultures adept oil pulling for the same purpose, with different oils.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is it possible to receive a free dessert at an Italian restaurant if you do not finish your meal?
Answer: TANSTAAFL, there ain’t no such thing as a free lunch. Even when restaurants offer you a dessert, a coffee or digestive drink, they do so because you already spent a fair amount of money. Italian restaurants are not run by demanding moms who expect you to finish your plate or meal. When drinks on a plane are free, people will drink, thirsty or not. When drinks have to be bought, few people seem to be interested. Though free drinks come with a more expensive ticket. Still, being offered a dessert is always nice. As is a cup of coffee on a plane.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is your favorite British dish and why do you enjoy it? Is it a common dish in your region?
Answer: No doubt about that. A piping hot shepherd’s pie. Pure comfort food. Wicked tongues may suggest it is an English take on the French hachis Parmentier. Have mercy on their souls. It is basically unheard of where I live, as ground lamb is hard to find. But when served, it is always a success. So it goes.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some easy Italian pasta dishes that can be made in a dorm?
Answer: The first authentic Italian pasta dishes I ever tried was prepared in a dorm by two Italian girls. They had taken it upon them to cook. Apart from a pack of pasta, some shrivelled garlic and a dash of olive oil, they had a jar of bell peppers at their disposal. The dorm kitchen had a pot, a pan and one burner, so what they brought to the table was absolutely stunning. They fried a little garlic in oil and added the bell peppers, cut in strips. After some simmering it was set aside. The fresh boiled pasta (next step) was added to the pan and put on on the stove again. Some thorough stirring and this was the result.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is pasta good for children or adults?
Answer: Pasta is good for adults and children alike. As carbs, in general, are. There are two aspects one should consider though: Don’t blame pasta when you are going to add terrible things. You may be adding fresh stuff to your pasta, but just prepare and eat too much. Consider that an average Italian portion of pasta weighs about 100g (3.4oz). Do you really think this would do you -or your children- any harm?

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the difference between fresh and dried pasta? Why do people still eat dried pasta if fresh pasta is considered to taste better?
Answer: All pasta is born fresh. The drying process may or may not follow. When endeavouring making pasta at home, it is hardly ever followed by a drying-stage. Industries on the other hand almost always dry pasta as it prolongs shelf life considerably. More expensive and artisanal brand will take their time doing so while run-off-the-mill pasta is exposed to high temperatures for a short time, and so eliminating most nutritious elements. As fresh pasta has to be prepared at the spot, it is more valuable, not per se better. Pasta comes with a condiment that will eventually define the outcome. In Italy fresh pasta is surely not a daily product; people prepare it for a special occasion, when they have time to do so.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the best way to make chickpeas?
Answer: Turning chickpeas in a snack is easy and very tasty. The general idea is to mix boiled and drained chickpeas with olive oil and spices before popping them in a hot oven for about half an hour. You can flavour your chickpeas as you please. A personal favourite is oil, salt and rosemary. Though oil, garlic powder, paprika is not easier to resist.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Would you use aloe in recipes?
Answer: In summer we prepare a quenching drink with aloe vera. The gel is mixed with water, lemon and a bit of sugar, topped off with granita. The slight bitterness of aloe matches the sourness of the lemon and sweetness of the granita.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the best way to cook fresh red bell peppers without burning them?
Answer: The best way to remove the skin from a bell pepper -whatever colour, not just the red ones - is indeed by burning it. Mainly out of laziness I leave the skin on. A preferite way is turning them into a peperonata. It is pretty easy, especially when not peeling the bell peppers. Fry an onion, add your bell pepper cut in strips. When tender, add tomato (or tomato sauce), vinegar and sugar. An excellent sweet sour antipasto.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What are some recipes from Portugal?
Answer: The Portuguese cuisine is seriously underrated. To savour this excellent cuisine, one has to travel there, as Portuguese restaurants are pretty uncommon. A dish I particularly like is their take on ‘surf and turf’ , pork meat with clams (carne de porco à Alentejano). Apart representing land and sea, the presence of potatoes, garlic, coriander and spices make it a unique dish that should be on your wish-to-eat list.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Can you share a recipe that includes both red onions and olives as ingredients?
Answer: Insalata vastasa, Sicilian potato salad. Apart from red onions and olives, this dish contains boiled potatoes, green beans and tomatoes, seasoned with olive oil and vinegar, and a generous dusting of origano. Insalata vastasa is indeed an easy dish to prepare, and even easier when you find yourself in Sicily, where all ingredients are sold at the greengrocer. Even more, they sell ready boiled green beans and potatoes. It is just a matter of assembling the ingredients.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the recommended sauce to pair with Italian sausage?
Answer: I’d recommend sausage in tomato sauce. Fry your sausage in pan, not worrying to cook it through. Then add tomato sauce and let it simmer away. You get two for the price of one: use the sauce to season your pasta and have sausages as secondo. Though there is no need, you can enrich the recipe by frying some onion first.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: How much sauce should be used for a large spaghetti dish?
Answer: In Italy the emphasis lays on pasta; pasta is eaten with sauce, not the other way around. There is no real possibility to actually quantify the amount of sauce that is added to pasta. More than the word ‘sauce’ Italians use the word condimento, seasoning. The reason is pretty straightforward: when you finish having your pasta, the plate should be empty, not having a lake of sauce laying there. So this looks like a bad joke While this is what you are supposed to be served: An average Italian portion of pasta is somewhere around 100g (3.5oz). Gigantic portions are not only bad for your health -in the long run- but also terribly boring. What’s the fun of eating from a trough?

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What dish is your city known for?
Answer: Italian dishes often have the extension of a city or region; alla Veneziana, alla Romana etc. For Palermo, that is alla Palermitana. Here are some examples: Probably not as know as the Milanese, but truly delicious. The cutlets are oiled and then breaded in a mix of breadcrumb, garlic, grated cheese (pecorino or caciocavallo), chopped parsley, salt and pepper. It stands out from other oven-baked pasta for the choice of pasta, little rings, and the presence of peas, boiled eggs and often fried eggplant. Panino ca meusa, a spleen (and lung) sandwich. The boiled and sliced offal meat is cooked in lard. It comes with grated cheese and lemon. Panino panelle e crocché, a sandwich with fried chickpea slabs and potato croquets Sfincione. Soft dough seasoned with anchovy, tomato sauce, onion (loads) and caciocavallo cheese. It may look like a nasty skin disease but tastes great

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What type of vegetable oil is commonly used in Italian cooking?
Answer: About 95% of Italians use olive oil. This does not mean they all use good, genuine oil, but still. I still have to meet an Italian who uses other but olive oil to season a salad. When it comes to frying, other oils are used; sunflower, peanut or mixed oils.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What's your go-to recipe for a quick and easy meal?
Answer: When having very little time or being extremely lazy, a fried egg is the solution. Preferably eaten from the pan with some bread.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is the best homemade dessert you made and you were very proud on how it turned out?
Answer: Being pretty hopeless with desserts, yesterdays concoction was something to be proud of. Gelo di caffè, coffee jelly. Half a litre of espresso coffee -made in a moka pot - agricultural rum (a generous splash), a stick of cinnamon, sugar (about 70g) and cornstarch (50g). Just before it boiled, we poured the liquid in moulds and let is set for a couple of hours in the fridge. Next time 1 litre of coffee.

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: Is there a difference in Italian cuisine between regions in Italy, or is there a standard way of cooking throughout the country?
Answer: Although it is true that the various regions tend to have proper dishes, these are complemented with standard dishes. The latter may have origin in one region but have become popular in the rest of the country. For example, lasagne are not just eaten in Emilia, and carbonara pasta is ubiquitous. It remains unlikely to find pasta with sardines in Trento or canoderli in Sicily. But then again, vis unita fortior, force united is stronger

Name: Ian De Pagie
Question: What is a unique food that you enjoy putting hot sauce on?
Answer: Pineapple goes wonderfully well with hot sauce, and so it does on mango.

Name: Ian De Pagie
